summary: Gone 1942 house and 1963 DNR live-in tower on Dow Mountain, Mason County, WA; a 1972 USGS note says the house was torn down and summit leveled.

facts.design: 1942: 12x24 ft house with half second story; 1963: 40-ft wooden DNR live-in tower
facts.status_note: The 1963 DNR tower is gone. By 1972 the house was torn down and the summit leveled, per USGS surveyors quoted in a trip report.

staffing.status: lookouts listed most summers 1955-1967; 1967 possibly the last staffed year

access.note: The signs at the Lake Cushman gate say driving the road beyond is for Lake Cushman Maintenance Company members. The trip report says nothing it found indicates hiking is banned, though one neighbor has complained about the web page. Part of the route is on private property.

visit.trail_note: About 3 miles and 1,800 ft of gain, starting at the Lake Cushman Maintenance Office. The summit is open but surrounded by trees.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 2,516 ft (767 m) for the site. The trip report gives 2,521 ft as the summit elevation. The story gives both and does not choose.
The trip report says the house was used as AWS station Charlie 3-3 in 1942. The Weebly page cites a May 1, 1944 AWS report that lists the station. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief elevation 766.9 m matches the register (767 m). Brief coordinates and FFLOS registration match; no corrections. The 1963 tower: register says it replaced the house; trip report says it was built beside the house and the house torn down within a few years. Trip report photo captions include 'Footing' with no text on location or date, so not used. Access level 'restricted' is from the gate sign and trip report; the trip report says hiking is not forbidden, but it was written by a hiker and a neighbor complaint is mentioned, so check with the Lake Cushman Maintenance Company before going. Staffing names omitted from story. No WebSearch used; four cached pages read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: 'at the summit' is changed to 'on the mountain' because the trip report does not place the platform at the summit. The gate sign restricts driving, not hiking, and the neighbor complaint is now noted. The staffing sentence now says 1967 may be the lookout's last year, matching the trip report.
